paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God is the LORD of the hills AND the valleys, and He doesn't need us to help Him prove it. The Arameans said He was "a god of the hills and not of the valleys," so the LORD said, "Then you will know that I am the LORD" (1 Kings 20:28). Moving the fight to the plains didn't change a thing. That's me trying to out-bake the oven by moving to a bigger kitchen. Same oven, same LORD, and the LORD wins.

Then comes the hard part. Ahab got a huge win that he didn't earn, and then he let go of the man the LORD had "devoted to destruction" (1 Kings 20:42). He called Ben-hadad his brother, made a treaty, and sent him away. I think Ahab felt like he was being gracious. But the LORD had said something different, and Ahab picked his own plan over the LORD's word. I think this one hurts, because it shows how a person can get a big gift from God and still not listen to Him.

So what's it for you, baker? When God has spoken, partial obedience is still not obeying. The first companion refused the LORD's word and paid for it (1 Kings 20:35-36), and Ahab left angry instead of humble (1 Kings 20:43). Don't just enjoy what God gives you. Listen to what He says, and do it when it's inconvenient, when it's awkward, and when your own plan looks nicer. And Ahab's story is far from done, so stay tuned.
